text:
rachel: Quick one — installed redwoodctl via the Windows MSI, then tried to use it from WSL. `redwoodctl auth login` opens the browser on Windows but WSL still shows not-authenticated.

ben: That's the expected pitfall: Windows exe writes creds to %LOCALAPPDATA%. From WSL you'll need the device flow or install the Linux binary in-distro.

rachel: Device flow worked, but it felt clunky to tell new hires to switch flows. Would be great if the installer offered a WSL shim option.

kai: Agreed. Proposal: `redwoodctl install --wsl-shim` that writes a tiny wrapper to `/usr/local/bin` calling the Windows exe via `/mnt/c/...`. Also add optional profile mirroring so `~/.redwood/profiles.json` is created when running under WSL.

rachel: Any race/permission concerns for mirroring?

kai: Mirror must use atomic write (write to tmp file then mv) and respect umask. We should avoid auto-sync without opt-in to prevent accidental overwrites when both sides write. Also add `redwoodctl config sync` to force a merge.

rachel: Sounds good. Can we also detect WSL automatically and prompt during install?

kai: Yes: detect via `/proc/version` or `WSL_INTEROP`. Prompt: "Detected WSL — create shim in /usr/local/bin and offer to mirror credentials to ~/.redwood (y/N)?". Not enabled by default.

dev-tools-bot: New ticket created: DEVEX-4510 — installer: offer WSL shim and profile mirroring. Assigned to @kai.

ben: Add a note to the Windows install docs: "If you use the Windows binary from WSL, prefer `redwoodctl auth login --device` or run the Linux package inside WSL."

rachel: Verified a quick dev build: shim + device flow works for me. Thanks all :rocket:
